r1_status.F-5: OPEN: pre-migration state records only specId, not the grader source or legacy spec path; after specs/ is deleted, r2 cannot both preserve that source and resume through the canonical case on another machine.
r1_status.F-9: OPEN: the projection is still incomplete and exact reconstruction fails because title is case-owned although several aliases have configuration-specific titles; environment.denyMechanism and environment.maven also appear in no row.
r1_status.F-10: OPEN: §10 still does not require schemas or normative field documentation for cohort records, proposal records, or compare results.

findings.claim: The §5 join cannot reconstruct all six aliases byte-for-byte because title is assigned wholly to the case, but legacy titles vary by configuration and are emitted into the contract. The permitted differences do not include title or contract intent text.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:119 assigns title to C; benchmark/provision.sh:561-566 emits manifest id and title into the contract; benchmark/specs/bm-1/manifest.json:4 has the base title while benchmark/specs/bm-2d/manifest.json:4 appends a Devin-roster qualifier; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:204-206 permits only ids, tag, and paths to differ.
findings.fix: Normalize the generated title intentionally and list that as a migration difference, or split case title from an optional configuration-specific run-title suffix and project both explicitly. Make the equivalence fixture compare the resulting Intent text.

findings.claim: The projection table does not cover every current manifest key: environment.denyMechanism and environment.maven occur in every manifest but appear in no row. Their prose is task policy, not configuration allowance, so an implementer must guess whether to discard or relocate it.
findings.evidence: benchmark/specs/bm-1/manifest.json:190-192 contains environment.denyMechanism and environment.maven; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:129 projects only environment.delegateNetwork and delegateNetworkReason, and §5 has no other environment row.
findings.fix: Project environment.denyMechanism and environment.maven verbatim into case-owned network/build-policy notes, or explicitly declare them retired documentation and update the byte-equivalence exclusions.

findings.claim: Legacy resume remains internally contradictory. R2 says the grader source is preserved as recorded, but schema-v1 state never recorded it; it records only specId, and the current resume path derives both manifest and grader from specs/<specId>. Deleting specs after checking only this machine cannot guarantee resumability on another machine.
findings.evidence: benchmark/run-cohort.sh:220-230 writes schema-v1 state with specId but no path or grader; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:253-270 reconstructs specs/<specId> and the legacy mission path; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:342-364 derives the grader from that manifest; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:160-166 promises preservation and checks only this machine before deletion; migration deletes specs at :207.
findings.fix: Define a schema-v1 resume adapter that preserves mission id and contract path but explicitly maps the legacy alias to the canonical case-version grader, and prove its bytes equal the former grader. Before deletion, require an inventory/drain protocol covering every trials root or retain the legacy directories indefinitely.

findings.claim: The case-version immutability digest is self-referential as specified: case.json records the digest, while any change to case.json changes the digested directory. No ordinary digest value can satisfy that definition, and the design does not define an excluded field or canonicalization.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:44-49 says any case.json change requires a new version and the directory content digest is recorded in case.json; acceptance at :246-248 requires that digest to validate.
findings.fix: Either remove the redundant digest and use the git object/tree identity, or define a canonical digest that excludes only case.json.contentDigest (while including all other normalized case.json bytes), file paths, modes, and content with unambiguous framing.

findings.claim: The instrument-tag digest algorithm is underspecified and the resulting ref has no stated length bound. Hashing unspecified 'instrument bytes' leaves file ordering, path names, mode bits, and concatenation framing to the implementer; the unbounded caseId and caseVersion can also create an invalid or uncreatable ref component.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:168-171 specifies only sha256 over instrument bytes; benchmark/provision.sh:181-186 currently validates identifier/version grammar but not total tag length; benchmark/provision.sh:536 and :632 create and push the tag.
findings.fix: Define a canonical bundle encoding containing sorted relative path, executable mode, byte length, and bytes for every declared instrument. Add schema length limits ensuring the complete tag is a valid git ref and filesystem-safe component, and validate with git check-ref-format before provisioning.

findings.claim: Allowing run-cohort.sh to select the newest case version is unsafe. A cohort is durable evidence and proposals name an explicit caseVersion, so an unpinned command can silently change meaning after a new version is added and can run a pair the proposal does not name, discovering the error only during comparison.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:172-179 makes proposal membership version-specific; :185-186 advertises an optional version for run-cohort; :193-194 selects newest when omitted; current benchmark/run-cohort.sh:193-230 persists the selected identity only after cohort creation, while compare.py:529-536 performs proposal/spec membership and installed-version checks later.
findings.fix: Require caseId@caseVersion for cohort starts, especially with --proposal. Keep newest-version resolution only for explicitly ad-hoc provisioning, or require an interactive/explicit --latest acknowledgement and reject it with --proposal.

findings.claim: The documentation plan still fails the another-machine test for evolution and result tooling because it mentions versioned identity, scorecard, proposal, and cohort schemas but migration creates only three new schemas, while §10 requires annotated examples only for cases and configurations and does not require a compare-result schema at all.
findings.evidence: benchmark currently has only benchmark/schemas/benchmark-identity.schema.json and benchmark/schemas/scorecard.schema.json; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:102 mentions proposal and cohort schemas; :198-201 adds only three new schemas; :213-224 specifies detailed examples only for case/configuration and merely links whatever schemas exist; :172-180 introduces schemaVersion-2 proposals and compare results.
findings.fix: Add and document versioned schemas for cohorts, proposals, and compare results, including schema-v1 read compatibility, required/optional fields, ancestry fields, and canonical pair membership. Include their validation commands in README procedures.

findings.claim: The content-digest immutability mechanism is unnecessary migration scope unless out-of-git case directories are supported. Git already makes historical case versions immutable by commit identity, while the proposed embedded digest adds canonicalization, line-ending, executable-bit, and version-bump failure modes unrelated to separating cases from configurations.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:44-49 adds a refusal mechanism; :196-209 makes it part of the migration; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:177-178 already pins evidence to a git candidate SHA.
findings.fix: Prefer validating that a named case version is committed and recording its git tree/object identity. Retain a separate instrument digest only for the tag. If embedded digests are required for exported kits, state that requirement and specify canonicalization fully.

summary: R2 closes most round-1 architecture findings: it honestly separates the two instrument versions, preserves strict comparison controls, versions proposals and results, makes host caps optional, splits network requirement from allowance, and fixes eligibility. It is not implementable without further decisions, however. Exact alias reconstruction still fails on configuration-specific titles and omitted environment fields; legacy resume promises data that old state never recorded; the case digest is self-referential; instrument hashing and ref length are underspecified; unpinned cohort versions can silently change experimental identity; and the another-machine documentation surface still omits cohort, proposal, and compare-result schemas. Mission id = caseId itself presents no current grammar or collision defect because targets are separate and taskrun satisfies the existing mission-id grammar, and the §6 rules admit all six legacy aliases.
